root_causes.description: product-catalog, a leaf service with no downstream dependencies, shows an intrinsic ~1000x increase in server-side p99 latency (baseline ~10ms -> ~10s) with zero errors and no CPU, memory, or restart changes. Every other high-latency service (frontend, recommendation, checkout) calls product-catalog, so their latency is propagated from it.

recommendation's server p99 latency rose from a flat 4.97ms to ~4,970ms during the window. Because recommendation depends on product-catalog (topology: recommendation -> product-catalog), this is most consistent with downstream propagation rather than an intrinsic fault.

frontend is the user-facing aggregator that depends directly on product-catalog (and on recommendation/checkout which also call it). Its p99 latency rose from ~40ms to ~5,661ms during the window, consistent with aggregation of propagated product-catalog latency rather than a primary fault.

evidence.observed_value: frontend search_traces (service_name=frontend, min_duration_ms=5000): p95_duration=661200ms, 0 errors; top operation user_get_recommendations=16602ms
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend p95 duration in low tens of ms pre-incident

remediation_steps: Inspect the product-catalog deployment for an injected latency fault or slow code path, since its SERVER span p99 jumped ~1000x to ~10s at 14:05:55 while CPU, memory, restarts and error rate stayed normal.
Check product-catalog for thread/connection starvation or artificially delayed handlers (e.g. chaos or flagd latency injection targeting product-catalog) and roll back the causing change.
Restart/roll the product-catalog pods to clear the condition and verify p99 returns to ~10ms.
Confirm recovery propagates: recommendation, checkout and frontend p99 should fall back toward ~5ms / ~25ms / ~40ms respectively.
Add a p99 latency SLO alert on product-catalog server spans (leaf dependency), since it acts as a single latency-amplification point for frontend, recommendation and checkout.
